text:
[Subject] Extremely disappointed with the impolite and unprofessional behavior of the nursing staff.
Today, I brought my child, who has been ill for over a month, to see a doctor at this clinic. My husband came into the examination room with us, but unfortunately, he didn't understand the doctor's exact diagnosis.
While waiting to pay, I politely asked the nurse at the counter what exactly was wrong with my child. At first, she brushed it off, saying "just a cold." When I explained that the symptoms didn't seem like just a common cold and asked her to double-check with the doctor, her response was completely unacceptable. Instead of responding professionally, she acted very rudely, waving her hand dismissively and telling me to "go back and wait."
Later, another nurse came out and said something in Thai (which I later learned was about allergic rhinitis). Since I don't speak Thai fluently, I handed her my phone with a translation app so she could speak into it so I could understand my child's symptoms correctly. But shockingly, when she was about to speak, she stopped, waved her hand dismissively again, pointed at my husband, and refused to communicate directly with me.
As a mother who is very concerned about her child's health, I was treated as if I didn't exist and was a nuisance, simply because of the language barrier. Using a hand to swat away worried parents is extremely disrespectful and completely unacceptable in any medical facility.
I urge management to investigate this behavior and provide your staff with thorough training on basic etiquette, empathy, and how to communicate respectfully with foreign patients. I expect a medical clinic to provide "care," not "disrespect."
